title: Impact of Decline in Private Investments on Job Creation and Business Competitiveness
what_it_is: Impact of Decline in Private Investments on Job Creation and Business Competitiveness

sections.label: Questions on investment and jobs
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Trade and Industry about falling private investments, firm closures, competitiveness, productivity, business costs, and job creation from investment commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) how is the Government addressing the sharp fall in private investments which have been contracting for the past two and a half years; (b) what is the Government doing to check the rising number of firm closures this year; and (c) how will falling private investments and economic restructuring affect job creation in the medium term.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) how is the Government helping companies to remain competitive in the global market; (b) whether there are improvements in productivity across various sectors; and (c) whether the Ministry has looked into how local price increases	– from labour, materials, transport to a stronger Singapore dollar – are impacting on the overall business cost.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) what has been the achievement rates of expected jobs creation from investment commitments made in the last five years; (b) whether an under-supply of suitable manpower was a factor affecting investment commitments at any point during that period; and (c) whether the Ministry anticipates challenges in the supply of manpower to fill the 16,800 jobs that EDB has reported that its 2015 	Page: 27 investment commitments are expected to create.

sections.label: Falling tariffs and rental indices
sections.summary: Regulated household tariffs fell 24% from early last year to second quarter 2016, and industrial, office and retail rental indices declined.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One reference point is the regulated tariffs that households pay because they are in a non-contestable market, and that have declined by 24% from the beginning of last year to the second quarter of 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Industrial rental index has decreased by 6.8% over the past five quarters.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For commercial rents, the office rental index in the central region fell by 12.2%, while the retail rental index also in the central region declined by 9.3% over the same period.

sections.label: WCL loan catalysis
sections.summary: The WCL is expected to catalyse more than S$2 billion of loans over the next three years and complements existing loan schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The WCL is expected to catalyse more than S$2 billion of loans over the next three years, and complements existing loan schemes.

sections.label: Manpower efforts and job commitments
sections.summary: Interventions include curriculum development, training with Institutes of Higher Learning, and company apprenticeships, aligned with SkillsFuture; EDB expects 2016 investment commitments to create 20,000 to 22,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Specific interventions include curriculum development for pre-employment training (PET), continuing education and training (CET) with local Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), as well as partnerships with companies to provide apprenticeships and other applied learning opportunities for our students.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: These manpower efforts are aligned with our national SkillsFuture movement, which aims to prepare Singaporeans for jobs of the future, with a judicious complement of foreign manpower to address any skills gaps in the short to medium term.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For 2016, EDB expects investment commitments to create 20,000 to 22,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This represents an increase in job commitments, compared to 16,800 in 2015 and 18,600 in 2014.

sections.label: Investment figures correction
sections.summary: The speaker states it is not a decline of $10 billion, citing $12.1 billion in 2013 and $11.5 billion in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is not a decline of $10 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I said $12.1 billion in 2013 and $11.5 billion in 2015.

sections.label: Micron semiconductor investment
sections.summary: Members would have read about Micron's commitment, which has substantial investment in semiconductor manufacturing in wafer fabrication, part of Singapore's electronics cluster.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In recent times, Members would have read about the commitment by Micron, which has a substantial investment in semi-conductor manufacturing in the wafer fabrication sector, which is an important part of our electronics cluster in Singapore.

sections.label: AbbVie facility opening
sections.summary: The speaker opened a facility by AbbVie, a bio-pharmaceutical company producing biological treatments for cancers and other diseases.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I have said, just a couple of weeks back, I opened a facility by AbbVie, a bio-pharmaceutical company producing state-of-the-art biological treatments for cancers and various other disease conditions.

sections.label: Job creation data
sections.summary: The speaker says job creation data shows jobs continue to be created and are adequate for Singaporeans' needs and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If you look at the job creation data that I have shared, we continue to create jobs and there are adequate jobs in many ways to meet the needs and aspirations of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Securing investments and skillsets
sections.summary: The speaker describes securing investments and opportunities, and working with universities and institutions to provide needed skillsets, including targeted modular programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The first is securing the investments and the opportunities so that we actually have a pipeline that Singaporeans can benefit from.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The second is to work upstream with our Universities and Institutions of Higher Learning to make sure that the skillsets that are needed are being provided, not just through three-year degree programmes or diploma programmes but even, if necessary, doing some targeted modular programmes which is what we do collectively between MTI and MOM, and our agencies like EDB working with WDA, MOE and the institutions.

sections.label: Jobs for mature workers
sections.summary: The speaker says it is harder to do but important, and has made the point that many jobs can be taken up by mature workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Harder to do, but it is something that is very important and that is why I have made the point that many of the jobs can actually be taken up by mature workers.

sections.label: Net enterprise formation figures
sections.summary: In the first and second quarters of this year, net enterprise formation was positive, at 2,001 and 9,000 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In fact, in the first and second quarters of this year, there was net enterprise formation, positive.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It was actually not an insignificant number, it was 2,001 for the first quarter and 9,000 in the second quarter.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps sectors
sections.summary: Industry Transformation Maps are being developed for 23 sectors, which the speaker says have been talked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: First, the Industry Transformation Maps are being developed for 23 sectors which we have talked about.
